neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, calming environment, opportunity for sensory exploration

activity_title: Embark on a scavenger hunt for different types of leaves and flowers
instruction: Take a stroll through your backyard or local area and collect different types of leaves and flowers. Aim for at least 5 unique specimens, and take a moment to observe their colors and shapes.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible pace, sensory-rich experience, encourages exploration without strict guidelines

activity_title: Create rock cairns by stacking stones in the forest
instruction: Find a variety of stones in the forest and stack them carefully to create a rock cairn. Take your time to balance each stone and enjoy the process.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with natural materials, repetitive motion, and no strict time limits can be soothing.

activity_title: Set out on a mindful nature walk
instruction: Take a walk in nature and pay attention to the different textures and colors around you, noticing how they make you feel.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages sensory exploration at your own pace, flexible and calming environment

activity_title: Sit and meditate in nature
instruction: Find a quiet spot outside, sit comfortably, and close your eyes. Take deep breaths and listen to the natural sounds around you for 10-20 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle sensory input, no time pressure, calming environment

activity_title: Collect natural materials and make a seasonal nature display
instruction: Take a walk outdoors to gather pinecones, acorns, and other natural materials. Arrange them in a bowl or on a tray to create a beautiful seasonal display.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle sensory experience, encourages exploration and creativity, no strict time limits

activity_title: Walk a nearby hill or slope
instruction: Challenge yourself to walk a nearby hill or slope to give your legs a gentle workout. Take your time and enjoy the view as you go.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle physical activity, allows for personal pacing, and offers a change of scenery.

activity_title: Construct a simple bug hotel
instruction: Gather twigs, leaves, and small logs. Stack them in a sheltered spot in your garden or yard, creating small spaces for bugs to hide and thrive.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with natural materials, flexible structure, and calming outdoor environment

activity_title: Identify wildflowers with a guidebook
instruction: Locate a wildflower patch in your area and use a local guidebook to identify different species, taking notes or sketching your favorites.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature can be soothing, but the activity may require focus and attention to detail.

activity_title: Visit a local pond or stream to observe aquatic wildlife and sketch what you see
instruction: Take a sketchbook and some pencils, find a quiet spot by the water, and spend time observing the plants and animals around you. Capture what you see in your sketchbook.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle sensory experience, flexible timing, encourages focus and observation

activity_title: Draw a detailed self-portrait using a mirror
instruction: Set up a mirror in a well-lit area and use any drawing tools you have at home to create a detailed self-portrait. Take your time to observe your features and express yourself on paper.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages self-expression, allows for personal pacing, and provides a calming focus on details.

activity_title: Illustrate the view from your window
instruction: Grab some paper and colored pencils or paints, then sit by your window and carefully sketch or paint the landscape or cityscape you see, focusing on the details that catch your eye.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible timing, allows for personal expression, calming focus on the visual details

activity_title: Draw a comic strip inspired by a funny event or story from your life
instruction: Think of a funny story from your life, then sketch a simple comic strip with 4-6 panels illustrating the key moments. Use stick figures and speech bubbles to bring your story to life.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible structure, allows for creativity, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Create a series of abstract shapes and patterns
instruction: Grab some paper and your favorite drawing tools. Start by making random shapes, then fill them in with different textures and shading techniques to explore your creativity.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible approach, encourages self-expression, no right or wrong way to create

activity_title: Design a new piece of clothing by sketching an outfit
instruction: Grab a sketchbook and colored pencils. Start by drawing the outline of your outfit, then add intricate details and colors to bring your design to life.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible pacing, encourages creativity, visual and tactile engagement

activity_title: Draw a map of your ideal fictional world
instruction: Grab some paper and colored pencils, then let your imagination flow as you sketch landscapes and landmarks that exist only in your mind.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible structure, encourages creativity, low pressure, and can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Make a color wheel by drawing and coloring sectors with different shades and tints
instruction: Draw a large circle and divide it into 12 equal sections. Use different colors to fill each section, experimenting with shades and tints by adding white or black to your base colors.
neurodivergent_notes: Creative expression with visual stimulation, flexible pacing, and no strict outcomes

activity_title: Doodle a whimsical animal character
instruction: Grab some paper and colored pencils, then let your imagination run wild as you create a unique animal character with special features and a fun personality.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible and open-ended, allowing for personal expression without strict guidelines.

activity_title: Sketch a botanical illustration focusing on a single plant species
instruction: Choose a single plant species and observe its distinct features. Use a pencil to lightly sketch the outline, then add details like leaves and flowers, and finish with color if you like.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages focus and observation, flexible pacing, and can be done in a quiet space

activity_title: Perform ankle rolls while sitting
instruction: While seated, lift one foot off the ground and roll your ankle in a circular motion for 10-15 seconds in each direction. Switch to the other foot and repeat.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, easy to follow, can be done anywhere, helps release tension

activity_title: Do calf raises for lower leg strength
instruction: Stand up and do 10 calf raises while holding onto a chair for balance to strengthen your lower legs.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and repetitive movement, can be done at your own pace, provides a gentle physical challenge

activity_title: Practice arm circles
instruction: Extend your arms out to the sides and make small circles forward for 30 seconds, then switch to backward circles for another 30 seconds to loosen your shoulder joints.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and repetitive movement, easy to integrate into a walk, promotes body awareness

activity_title: Neck Stretching for Relief
instruction: Gently tilt your head from side to side and forward to stretch the neck muscles and relieve stiffness. Repeat for 2-3 minutes, breathing deeply.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and quick, allows for focus on body awareness, can be done anywhere without equipment

activity_title: Seated Hamstring Stretch
instruction: Sit on the floor with one leg extended and the other bent. Reach towards your toes on the extended leg, feeling the stretch in your hamstring. Hold for 20-30 seconds and switch legs.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, easy to follow, can be done in a quiet space for focus.

activity_title: Complete a 10-minute session of toe taps while seated
instruction: Sit comfortably in a chair with your feet flat on the floor. Lift your right foot and tap your toes on the ground for 5 seconds, then switch to your left foot and repeat. Alternate feet for a total of 10 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and repetitive movement, easy to follow, can be done at your own pace.

activity_title: Gentle Spine Twist
instruction: Lie flat on the floor, bring one knee over to the opposite side of your body, and hold for a few breaths to feel a gentle stretch in your spine.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple movement, low sensory input, can be done anytime to relieve tension

activity_title: Do seated cat-cow stretches
instruction: Sit comfortably with your feet flat on the ground. Inhale, arch your back and lift your chest (cat), then exhale, round your back and tuck your chin (cow). Repeat this flow for 5-10 breaths.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, easy to follow, can be done anywhere, helps with body awareness

activity_title: Complete a set of wall push-ups
instruction: Stand facing a wall, place your hands shoulder-width apart on the wall, and slowly bend your elbows to lean your body towards the wall, then push back to the starting position. Aim for 10-15 repetitions.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, low strain on wrists, can be done at your own pace.

activity_title: Gentle Side Bends for Torso Loosening
instruction: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, raise your arms overhead, and gently bend to the right, then to the left, repeating each side 5 times to loosen your torso and waist.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple movements, no equipment needed, can be done anywhere, promotes body awareness

activity_title: Beginner's sun salutation sequence
instruction: Sun salutations are a flowing sequence of yoga poses done in rhythm with your breath. Start standing, raise your arms overhead, fold forward, step back into a plank, lower to the ground, push up into a gentle backbend, and return to standing — repeat 3-5 times to energize your morning.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movements, predictable sequence, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Practice the tree pose in your backyard
instruction: Stand tall, shift your weight to one leg, and place the sole of your other foot on your inner thigh or calf. Bring your hands to your heart and hold for 1-2 minutes, then switch sides.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, calming focus, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Perform a gentle seated forward fold
instruction: Sit with your legs extended in front of you, inhale deeply, and as you exhale, fold forward gently, reaching towards your toes while breathing deeply into the stretch.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, calming breath, easy to modify for comfort

activity_title: Engage in a restorative child's pose session
instruction: Kneel on the floor, sit back on your heels, and stretch your arms forward on the ground, resting your forehead down. Hold this position for 5-10 minutes to relax and release tension in your lower back.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, calming position, easy to modify for comfort

activity_title: Try a gentle warrior pose sequence
instruction: Stand tall and take a deep breath. Step your left foot back, bend your right knee, and extend your arms out to the sides. Hold for 5 breaths, then switch sides and repeat.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, focus on breath, adaptable pace, calming environment

activity_title: Practice deep breathing in a seated lotus position
instruction: Sit comfortably in a lotus position, close your eyes, and take deep breaths in through your nose for a count of four, then exhale slowly through your mouth for a count of six. Continue this for 5 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle and calming practice, easy to follow, can be done anywhere, promotes focus and relaxation

activity_title: Engage in a guided meditation while holding the mountain pose
instruction: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms at your sides. Close your eyes and take deep breaths while focusing on your posture. Listen to a guided meditation for 10-15 minutes to enhance mindfulness.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle guidance, predictable structure, calming environment, focus on breath and posture

activity_title: Perform a reclining twist on each side
instruction: Lie on your back with arms out to the sides. Bend your knees and let them fall to one side while keeping your shoulders on the ground. Hold for 5 breaths, then switch sides.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, easy to follow, can be done in nature for calming effects

activity_title: Balance in Eagle Pose
instruction: Stand on one foot, wrap the opposite leg around it, and cross your arms at the elbows. Hold this position for 1 minute, then switch sides to challenge your focus and coordination.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple movement, can be done anywhere, encourages mindfulness and focus

activity_title: Practice legs-up-the-wall pose
instruction: Lie on your back and scoot your hips close to a wall, then extend your legs up the wall for 10 minutes, allowing your arms to rest by your sides or on your belly.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle and calming, can be done in a quiet space, no complex instructions or equipment needed

activity_title: Bake a simple loaf of soda bread
instruction: In a bowl, mix 4 cups of flour, 1 teaspoon of baking soda, and 1 teaspoon of salt. Gradually stir in 1 and 1/2 cups of buttermilk until a dough forms. Shape into a loaf and bake at 425 degrees Fahrenheit for 30-35 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple, repetitive steps with a focus on sensory engagement and no strict time limits.

activity_title: Make jam from seasonal fruits
instruction: Gather seasonal fruits from a local farm or market, then wash, chop, and cook 4 cups of fruit with 2 cups of sugar and the juice of 1 lemon over medium heat until thickened, about 20-30 minutes. Pour into sterilized jars and let cool.

activity_title: Make handmade pasta from scratch
instruction: Mix 2 cups of flour with 3 large eggs and a pinch of salt, knead the dough for about 10 minutes until smooth, then roll it out thinly and cut into your desired shape.
neurodivergent_notes: Hands-on activity with a focus on texture and rhythm, may require breaks for sensory processing.

activity_title: Create your own spice blend
instruction: Gather herbs and spices you have at home, mix 1 tablespoon of each to create a unique seasoning, and taste as you go to adjust flavors.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible process, encourages creativity, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Create a homemade pizza
instruction: Mix 2 cups of flour, 1 packet of yeast, 1 teaspoon of salt, and 3/4 cup of warm water to form a dough. Let it rise for 30 minutes, then roll out and top with your favorite sauce, cheese, and toppings before baking at 475°F for 12-15 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Hands-on activity with flexible choices, engaging textures, and no strict time limits.

activity_title: Organize a neighborhood cookie swap
instruction: Bake a dozen cookies using your favorite recipe, then invite your neighbors to bring their own baked goods to share and exchange with each other.
neurodivergent_notes: Social interaction can be adjusted to comfort level, baking is a familiar and calming activity.

activity_title: Prepare an elaborate, three-course meal using only the ingredients you already have in your pantry
instruction: Take stock of your pantry and choose ingredients for a starter, main course, and dessert. Plan your dishes, then cook each course one at a time, savoring the process and creativity involved.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexibility in choosing ingredients and pacing, but may involve multiple steps and sensory input

activity_title: Host a potluck dinner
instruction: Invite friends over for a potluck dinner where each guest brings a homemade dish. Coordinate to ensure a variety of flavors and dietary preferences.
neurodivergent_notes: Social gathering may require planning and communication, which can be overwhelming for some.

activity_title: Spend a day marinating and slow-cooking a roast
instruction: Marinate a roast in your favorite spices and herbs for at least 4 hours. Then, slow-cook it in a covered pot with vegetables like carrots and potatoes for 6-8 hours on low heat until tender.
neurodivergent_notes: The process can be broken down into manageable steps, allowing for flexibility and creativity in seasoning.

activity_title: Try a traditional regional recipe
instruction: Research a traditional recipe from a specific region, gather the ingredients, and cook it while reflecting on its cultural background and cooking method.
neurodivergent_notes: Research phase allows for flexibility, cooking can be adjusted to personal pace

activity_title: Plan and take a day-long hike in a local nature reserve or park
instruction: Choose a local nature reserve or park, pack a lunch with sandwiches, fruit, and water, and enjoy a scenic picnic during your hike. Aim for a route that takes 4-6 hours to complete.
neurodivergent_notes: Nature provides soothing sensory input, but plan for breaks and have a flexible schedule.

activity_title: Collect and identify wildflowers during a nature walk
instruction: Take a nature walk and collect wildflowers you find along the way. When you get home, press them between the pages of an old book to preserve their beauty.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature can be soothing, and the activity allows for flexibility in pace and exploration.

activity_title: Organize a birdwatching expedition
instruction: Gather a small group of friends and head to a nearby park with binoculars and a bird guidebook. Aim to spot and identify at least ten different bird species during your time outdoors.
neurodivergent_notes: Structured activity with social interaction, calming nature sounds, and visual engagement.

activity_title: Build a fairy house using natural materials
instruction: Spend an afternoon collecting twigs, leaves, and stones during a walk in the woods, then assemble them into a whimsical fairy house using your imagination.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature, flexible creativity, and a calming environment.

activity_title: Roll down a nearby hill
instruction: Find a gentle hill, sit at the top, and roll down safely while enjoying the sensation of movement and the breeze on your skin.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and fun activity with sensory engagement, encourages exploration and movement.

activity_title: Take part in a local tree-planting event
instruction: Join a community tree-planting event, grab a sapling, dig a hole about twice the size of the root ball, place the tree in, and cover the roots with soil while gently patting it down.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging in nature, social interaction, and physical activity can be soothing and grounding.

activity_title: Explore the trails of a local botanical garden or arboretum
instruction: Spend the day wandering through the various trails of a local botanical garden or arboretum, taking time to observe the plants and flowers around you.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible pacing, natural surroundings, opportunities for quiet reflection

activity_title: Host a leaf-collecting and collage-making session
instruction: Gather a variety of leaves from your backyard or a nearby park, then arrange and glue them onto a piece of paper to create a beautiful collage.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature can be soothing, and the activity allows for creative expression without strict guidelines.

activity_title: Organize a community nature cleanup day
instruction: Gather friends and neighbors to pick up litter and debris in a local green space. Bring trash bags, gloves, and refreshments to share after the cleanup.
neurodivergent_notes: Structured activity with clear tasks, social interaction, and a focus on nature

activity_title: Forage for mushrooms or wild herbs
instruction: Spend a morning in a local forest, carefully identifying mushrooms or wild herbs. Bring a guidebook or use a reliable app to ensure safety and proper identification.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature can be soothing, but ensure clear identification steps to avoid overwhelm.

activity_title: Design and plant a vegetable garden
instruction: Choose a sunny corner in your backyard, select easy-to-grow seasonal vegetables like tomatoes, lettuce, and radishes, and plant them in rows with 12 inches apart. Water them well and watch them grow.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature, predictable routine, and sensory-rich experience can be soothing.

activity_title: Construct raised beds for your garden
instruction: Spend your weekend building raised beds by cutting wood into 4 pieces of 2x4 feet for the sides and 2 pieces of 2x2 feet for the corners, then assemble them with screws and fill with soil for planting.
neurodivergent_notes: Clear steps and physical activity can be grounding; consider breaking tasks into smaller parts.

activity_title: Learn to propagate houseplants by taking cuttings
instruction: Take a healthy cutting from an existing houseplant, about 4-6 inches long, remove the lower leaves, and place it in a glass of water or a pot with soil. Change the water every few days or keep the soil moist until roots develop.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple, repetitive task with clear steps, allows for gradual progress and observation.

activity_title: Spend an afternoon weeding and mulching your garden beds
instruction: Pull out weeds by hand or with a garden tool, then spread a layer of mulch around your plants to help retain moisture and suppress new weeds. Aim for a 2-3 inch layer of mulch.
neurodivergent_notes: Repetitive motions, connection with nature, and the rhythm of weeding can be soothing.

activity_title: Start a compost bin using kitchen scraps and yard waste
instruction: Collect kitchen scraps like vegetable peels and yard waste such as leaves and grass clippings. Layer them in a bin, keeping it moist and turning it every few weeks to create rich compost for your garden.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with natural materials, flexible timing, and a repetitive process can be soothing.

activity_title: Create a butterfly or bee-friendly garden plot
instruction: Choose a sunny spot in your yard or balcony and plant native flowers like lavender, coneflowers, and milkweed to attract butterflies and bees. Water them regularly and watch your garden come to life.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature can provide calming sensory experiences and a sense of accomplishment.

activity_title: Organize a plant swap with friends and neighbors
instruction: Invite friends and neighbors to bring cuttings and small plants to exchange. Set up a table where everyone can display their plants and enjoy chatting while you swap.
neurodivergent_notes: Social interaction can be flexible, and the activity allows for personal choice in plant selection.

activity_title: Construct a simple trellis or plant support
instruction: Gather some bamboo stakes or strong twine and create a support structure by tying the twine between the stakes in a grid pattern, allowing climbing vegetables to latch on as they grow.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple, clear steps with a focus on tactile engagement and outdoor setting, allowing for flexibility in pace.

activity_title: Host a garden tea party
instruction: Set up a cozy spot among your plants, brew some tea, and prepare homemade goodies like scones or finger sandwiches. Invite friends to enjoy the treats and share gardening tips together.
neurodivergent_notes: Social interaction can be overwhelming for some; consider a small group and a quiet setting.

activity_title: Create a sand tray for mindfulness
instruction: Fill a shallow tray with sand and use your fingers or small tools to draw patterns, allowing your mind to focus on the texture and movement.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging and calming sensory experience, flexible duration, encourages creativity and focus

activity_title: Make homemade play dough and sculpt figures
instruction: In a bowl, mix 2 cups of flour, 1 cup of salt, 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil, and 2 cups of water. Stir until smooth, then knead for a few minutes. Once ready, create fun shapes and figures with your hands.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging tactile experience, flexible timing, and creative expression without pressure.

activity_title: Explore textures with warm water and river stones
instruction: Fill a basin with warm water and smooth river stones, then use your feet to explore the textures and motion of the stones as you gently move them around.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle sensory experience, can be calming and grounding, allows for exploration at your own pace

activity_title: Wrap yourself in a weighted blanket and practice deep breathing
instruction: Find a quiet spot, wrap yourself in a weighted blanket, and take deep breaths in for a count of 4, hold for 4, and exhale for 6. Repeat for 5-10 minutes, focusing on the sensation of the blanket and your breath.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle sensory input, predictable routine, calming environment

activity_title: Create a sensory bin with natural objects
instruction: Collect small, natural objects like pinecones and acorns, and place them in a bin for calming, tactile exploration. Spend a few minutes feeling and sorting the items.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle sensory input, encourages exploration at one's own pace, no time constraints

activity_title: Engage in a blindfolded taste test
instruction: Gather a variety of small food items, blindfold yourself, and taste each one slowly, focusing on the flavors and textures. Try to guess what each item is.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages focus on sensory input, can be done at your own pace, adaptable to preferences

activity_title: Braid long grasses or twine into simple bracelets
instruction: Gather long grasses or twine, then take three strands, tie a knot at one end, and braid them together, repeating until you reach the desired length. Tie off the end to finish your bracelet.
neurodivergent_notes: Repetitive motion can be soothing, and the tactile experience is calming.

activity_title: Knead and shape homemade bread dough
instruction: Combine 3 cups of flour, 1 packet of yeast, 1 teaspoon of salt, and 1 cup of warm water in a bowl. Knead the dough for about 10 minutes until smooth, then shape it into a loaf and let it rise for 1 hour before baking.
neurodivergent_notes: Repetitive motions can be soothing, and the process is flexible with no strict timing.

activity_title: Perform ankle circles while standing
instruction: Stand tall and lift one foot slightly off the ground. Rotate your ankle in a circular motion, making 10 circles in one direction and then 10 in the opposite direction. Switch to the other foot and repeat.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and repetitive movement, can be done anywhere, promotes body awareness

activity_title: Practice a tree pose sequence
instruction: Stand tall and lift your arms overhead, then shift your weight to one leg and lift the other foot to your inner thigh or calf. Hold for 5 breaths, then switch legs.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, grounding exercise, can be done in a quiet space, promotes focus

activity_title: Invite a friend for an alfresco picnic and prepare simple sandwiches
instruction: Gather your favorite sandwich ingredients like bread, cheese, and veggies. Meet your friend at a park, lay out a blanket, and work together to make delicious sandwiches while enjoying the fresh air.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible timing, social interaction, and sensory-rich environment with nature sounds and smells

activity_title: Hike a local trail and collect interesting stones or leaves for your at-home nature display
instruction: Find a nearby trail, hike for at least 30 minutes, and gather unique stones or leaves that catch your eye to create a nature display at home.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature can be soothing, and the activity allows for personal pacing and exploration.

activity_title: Challenge yourself with a Sudoku puzzle book for a mental workout
instruction: Grab a Sudoku puzzle book and set a timer for 20 minutes. Start with an easy puzzle and work your way up to more challenging ones as you gain confidence.
neurodivergent_notes: Structured activity with clear goals, flexible pacing, and engaging problem-solving.

activity_title: Create a small wooden birdhouse using scrap wood and basic hand tools

activity_title: Do a series of gentle neck stretches to relieve tension
instruction: Sit or stand comfortably, slowly tilt your head to the right, bringing your ear toward your shoulder. Hold for 15 seconds, then switch to the left side. Next, gently nod your head forward and backward, and finally, turn your head to the right and left, holding each position for 15 seconds.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movements, easy to follow, can be done anywhere, promotes relaxation

activity_title: Try a sun salutation series in your garden or backyard

neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement with a predictable flow, can be done at your own pace in a calming outdoor setting

activity_title: Bake a loaf of homemade bread from scratch

neurodivergent_notes: Hands-on activity with clear steps, can be done at your own pace, engaging sensory experience

activity_title: Take a leisurely nature walk and identify different bird species
instruction: Stroll through your local park, take your time, and observe the birds around you. Use a bird identification app or a field guide to help you recognize different species as you enjoy the fresh air.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle pace, engaging with nature, no strict structure, allows for breaks and exploration

activity_title: Solve a crossword puzzle with a friend
instruction: Grab a crossword puzzle and sit down with a friend. Take turns filling in the answers, discussing clues, and enjoying the challenge together.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging and flexible activity, can be done at your own pace, promotes social interaction

activity_title: Knit a simple scarf using yarn you have at home

neurodivergent_notes: Repetitive motions can be soothing, and you can work at your own pace without pressure.

activity_title: Perform seated calf raises
instruction: While sitting, lift your heels off the ground, keeping your toes planted, and hold for a moment before lowering back down. Repeat for 10-15 reps to strengthen your lower legs.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple, repetitive movement that can be done anywhere, allowing for focus on breath and body.

activity_title: Practice a five-minute meditation sitting in the lotus position
instruction: Find a quiet space, sit in the lotus position with your legs crossed, close your eyes, and focus on your breath for five minutes, letting thoughts drift away.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle focus on breath, short duration, can be done anywhere, promotes calmness

activity_title: Prepare a batch of cookies using a family recipe to share with neighbors
instruction: Gather your ingredients: 2 cups of flour, 1 cup of sugar, 1 cup of butter, 2 eggs, and 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract. Mix them together, scoop onto a baking sheet, and bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 10-12 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple steps with clear measurements, engaging sensory experience, and a rewarding outcome

activity_title: Visit a nearby nature reserve and record your observations in a nature journal
instruction: Take a stroll through a nearby nature reserve, observing plants and animals, and jot down your thoughts and sketches in a nature journal.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible timing, engaging with nature can be soothing, and journaling allows for personal expression.

activity_title: Gather friends for a puzzle race

neurodivergent_notes: Can be competitive; consider allowing breaks or a relaxed pace if needed.

activity_title: Whittle a small figure from a fallen branch
instruction: Find a fallen branch or piece of wood, use a small knife to carefully carve out a simple figure, taking your time to enjoy the process and the texture of the wood.

activity_title: Do hip circles to loosen your hips
instruction: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place your hands on your hips. Gently rotate your hips in a circular motion, making 10 circles in one direction and then 10 in the opposite direction.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple movement, easy to follow, can be done anywhere, helps relieve tension

activity_title: Practice yoga nidra for deep relaxation
instruction: Find a quiet space, lie down comfortably, and close your eyes. Focus on your breath and allow your body to relax, letting go of tension for 20 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle guidance, calming environment, adaptable duration, promotes relaxation

activity_title: Cook a simple homemade soup with vegetables from your local farmers market
instruction: Gather fresh vegetables from your local farmers market, chop them into bite-sized pieces, and simmer in a pot with 4 cups of vegetable broth for 20-30 minutes. Season with salt, pepper, and your favorite herbs.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple steps, engaging sensory experience, flexible timing, and a rewarding outcome

activity_title: Explore a new hiking trail and take photos of unique natural features with a disposable camera
instruction: Find a local hiking trail, pack a disposable camera, and take your time exploring while capturing photos of interesting plants, rocks, or landscapes that catch your eye.

neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature can be soothing, and the activity allows for flexible pacing and exploration.

activity_title: Create and solve a challenging numerical puzzle
instruction: Draw a 3x3 grid and fill it with numbers 1 to 9 so that each row, column, and diagonal adds up to 15. Try to solve it in under 15 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging and structured task with clear goals, can be done at your own pace.

activity_title: Engage in a group brainstorming session to invent creative new logic puzzles or brain games
instruction: Gather a group of friends and spend 30 minutes brainstorming ideas for new logic puzzles or brain games. Use paper and pens to jot down your ideas and sketch out any concepts.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages collaborative thinking, may benefit from structured prompts to guide brainstorming

activity_title: Practice playing a new song on an acoustic guitar using only your ear
instruction: Choose a song you love, listen to it a few times, then try to pick out the melody on your acoustic guitar by ear. Start with a few notes and build up to the full melody.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages auditory processing, may require breaks to avoid frustration

activity_title: Organize a neighborhood jam session
instruction: Invite neighbors to bring their acoustic instruments and gather in a local park or backyard for a casual jam session. Set a time and encourage everyone to share a song or play together.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages social interaction but may require managing different personalities and noise levels.

activity_title: Learn a new scale on an instrument and improvise
instruction: Choose a scale on your wind or string instrument, practice it for 10 minutes, then create a simple improvisation using that scale for another 10 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible structure, allows for personal expression, can be calming or energizing depending on the scale chosen

activity_title: Build a basic didgeridoo out of PVC pipe and learn to play a simple rhythm
instruction: Cut a 1.5 to 2 meter long PVC pipe, seal one end with tape, and practice blowing into the open end while varying your mouth shape to create different sounds. Start with a simple rhythm like 'boom-chick' to get comfortable.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging and creative, allows for self-expression, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Compose an acoustic instrumental piece using only three chords
instruction: Choose three chords you love and create a simple melody by strumming or picking them in different sequences. Experiment with tempo and rhythm to find a sound that resonates with you.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible structure, encourages creativity, low pressure environment

activity_title: Create a musical story using percussive sounds from household items
instruction: Gather pots, pans, and other household items. Use wooden spoons or your hands to create rhythms and sounds, weaving them together to tell a story or express an emotion.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages creativity and self-expression, flexible and open-ended, engaging auditory input

activity_title: Teach yourself to play a simple folk song on the harmonica
instruction: Start by learning to blow and draw on the harmonica to create sound. Choose a simple folk song and practice playing it slowly, focusing on the melody and rhythm until you feel comfortable.
neurodivergent_notes: Repetitive practice can be soothing, but may require breaks to avoid frustration.

activity_title: Attend an open mic night and note different acoustic techniques
instruction: Find a local open mic night, sit back and listen to the performances while paying attention to different acoustic techniques used by the artists, such as vocal modulation and instrument resonance.
neurodivergent_notes: Can be overwhelming due to noise levels; choose a quieter venue if needed.

activity_title: Craft a set of homemade rhythm sticks
instruction: Gather two wooden dowels or sturdy sticks, each about 12 inches long. Decorate them with paint or washi tape, then use them to explore different beats and tempos by tapping them together or against surfaces.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging sensory activity with creative expression, allows for self-paced exploration

activity_title: Learn to fingerpick a tune on the ukulele using a songbook borrowed from the library
instruction: Find a songbook at your library, choose a simple song, and practice fingerpicking the melody on your ukulele. Start slowly, focusing on the rhythm and flow.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging and repetitive motions, allows for gradual learning at your own pace, can be calming and enjoyable

activity_title: Write a short song inspired by a recent event or personal experience
instruction: Sit in a comfortable spot with your instrument, reflect on a recent event or personal experience, and write down your thoughts and feelings in a simple song structure, using 2-3 verses and a chorus.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible structure allows for personal expression; may require breaks for processing thoughts.

activity_title: Compose lyrics to a melody you frequently hum or whistle
instruction: Think of a melody you often hum or whistle, then let your thoughts flow and write down lyrics that fit the rhythm and mood of the tune.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible and creative, allowing for personal expression without strict guidelines.

activity_title: Write a song using words from a favorite poem
instruction: Choose a favorite poem and select words from it to create your own song. Aim for a verse and a chorus, and let your creativity flow.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible structure, encourages creativity, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Create a parody song about a mundane household task
instruction: Think of a household task like washing dishes or folding laundry, then rewrite the lyrics of a popular song to humorously describe that task. Sing it out loud and have fun with it!
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages creativity with low pressure, can be done at your own pace, and allows for personal expression.

activity_title: Co-write a song with a friend
instruction: Sit with a friend and take turns writing lines or verses of a song without discussing the theme beforehand. Let your creativity flow and see where it takes you.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages creativity and collaboration, but may require flexibility in communication styles.

activity_title: Write a song in a genre you normally don't explore
instruction: Choose a genre like country or reggae, and spend 20-30 minutes writing lyrics and a simple melody. Use a guitar or piano if you have one, or just hum the tune.
neurodivergent_notes: Creative expression can be freeing, but may require breaks to avoid overwhelm.

activity_title: Develop a song over several days
instruction: Start with a simple melody or theme on day one, then add a new lyric or musical element each day for a week, allowing your creativity to flow.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages creative expression, can be done at your own pace, flexible structure

activity_title: Experiment with writing a song from the perspective of a historical figure
instruction: Choose a historical figure you admire, research their life, and write a song that expresses their thoughts and feelings about a significant event they experienced. Aim for 2-3 verses and a chorus.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible structure allows for personal expression, can be done at own pace.

activity_title: Craft a song using a random word from a dictionary
instruction: Open a dictionary, pick a random word, and write a short song or poem around that word, focusing on its meaning and emotions it evokes.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible structure allows for personal expression, minimal pressure, and encourages creativity.

activity_title: Write a lullaby tune and lyrics for a child in your life
instruction: Sit in a quiet space and think of a simple melody that feels soothing. Write down lyrics that express love and comfort, using simple words and phrases that resonate with the child.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle creative expression, no strict rules, flexible and personal approach

activity_title: Practice starting a fire with flint and steel
instruction: Gather flint, steel, and dry tinder. Strike the steel against the flint to create sparks, directing them onto the tinder until it catches fire. Enjoy the warmth and light of your fire pit.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging physical activity, requires focus and patience, can be calming with the right environment

activity_title: Learn to identify basic wild edibles and collect them for a salad
instruction: Take a walk in your local area and look for common wild edibles like dandelion greens, clover, or chickweed. Make sure to research beforehand to confirm they are safe to eat, then gently collect a handful for your salad.

activity_title: Experiment with different materials to construct an effective shelter in your backyard
instruction: Gather materials like branches, leaves, and tarps, then start building a shelter by creating a frame with branches and covering it with leaves or a tarp for protection from the elements.
neurodivergent_notes: Hands-on activity with flexible structure, allows for creativity and exploration, can be done at one's own pace

activity_title: Attend a wilderness survival workshop
instruction: Join a workshop to learn essential wilderness skills like fire-making and navigation. Bring a notebook to jot down tips and practice techniques with others.
neurodivergent_notes: May involve group activities and varying sensory inputs; check for accommodations in advance.

activity_title: Carve a small wooden tool from a fallen branch
instruction: Find a fallen branch, use a small knife to carefully carve out a simple tool shape, like a spatula or a hook, taking your time to enjoy the process.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature can be soothing; focus on the tactile experience and the rhythm of carving.

activity_title: Design a basic home-made water filter using natural materials found in your yard
instruction: Gather materials like sand, gravel, and charcoal from your yard. Layer them in a container, starting with gravel at the bottom, followed by sand, and then charcoal. Pour water through the filter and collect the clean water below.
neurodivergent_notes: Hands-on activity with clear steps, may require supervision for younger participants.

activity_title: Prepare a homemade first aid kit using bandanas, cotton, and other found materials
instruction: Gather bandanas, cotton, and any other materials you have at home like adhesive bandages, antiseptic wipes, or gauze. Arrange them in a small container or bag, ensuring you have essentials for minor injuries.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and clear steps, allows for personal customization, no rush involved

activity_title: Make a bow drill fire starter
instruction: Gather materials like a sturdy stick, a softer wood base, and a string or shoelace. Create a notch in the base, place the stick in the notch, and use the string to rotate the stick back and forth to create friction and spark a fire.
neurodivergent_notes: Hands-on activity with clear steps, may require patience and focus

activity_title: Master the art of knot-tying
instruction: Learn to tie essential survival knots like the bowline and square knot. Start with a length of rope about 3 feet long and practice tying each knot until you feel confident.
neurodivergent_notes: Clear, repeatable steps; tactile engagement; can be done at your own pace.

activity_title: Plan and conduct a 'no-cooking' day with raw foods
instruction: Choose a day to eat only raw or naturally prepared foods like fruits, vegetables, nuts, and seeds. Prepare a simple menu the night before, including snacks and meals that require no cooking.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible meal options, encourages mindful eating, no cooking stress

activity_title: Gather dandelion greens for a fresh salad
instruction: Head to a nearby field and carefully pick dandelion greens, making sure to choose young, tender leaves. Rinse them well and toss with your favorite dressing for a refreshing spring salad.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple, repetitive task with a focus on nature, allows for mindfulness and sensory engagement

activity_title: Identify and collect pine nuts from local pine trees
instruction: Find a local pine tree, look for pine cones, and gently shake or twist them to release the pine nuts. Roast the nuts in a pan over medium heat for 5-10 minutes until golden, then add them to your salad.

activity_title: Harvest wild blackberries or raspberries
instruction: Take a walk in nearby hedgerows and gently pick ripe blackberries or raspberries for a quick snack. Make sure to wash them before eating.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and enjoyable sensory experience, low pressure, and connection to nature

activity_title: Learn to discern edible mushrooms from non-edible ones with a local field guide
instruction: Grab a local field guide and head outdoors to identify mushrooms. Start by looking for common edible varieties and compare them with their non-edible counterparts, paying attention to color, shape, and habitat.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging visual and tactile experience, may require focus on details, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Pick wild mint to brew refreshing tea
instruction: Find wild mint in local fields or gardens, gently pluck a handful, rinse it, and steep in hot water for 5-10 minutes to enjoy a refreshing homemade tea.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple, sensory-rich experience with natural elements, encourages mindfulness without pressure.

activity_title: Collect and dry chamomile flowers for calming tea
instruction: Gently pick chamomile flowers from a garden or field, then lay them flat on a clean surface to dry for 3-5 days. Once dried, steep a handful of flowers in hot water for 5-10 minutes to enjoy a soothing tea.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature, simple repetitive task, calming sensory experience

activity_title: Safely forage and identify wild garlic or ramps for use in a nighttime stir-fry dish
instruction: Look for wild garlic or ramps in damp, shady areas. Identify them by their broad leaves and strong garlic smell. Harvest a handful, wash them, and chop to add to your stir-fry.
neurodivergent_notes: Clear identification steps, engaging sensory experience, may require focus on surroundings

activity_title: Seek out crab apples from neighborhood trees and make homemade jelly
instruction: Find crab apples from local trees, wash them, and cook with 4 cups of water and 1 cup of sugar until soft. Strain the mixture through a cheesecloth, then boil the juice for 10 minutes before pouring into sterilized jars.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature, clear steps, and a creative outcome can be soothing and rewarding.

activity_title: Discover sassafras trees and make tea
instruction: Take a walk on a nearby trail to find sassafras trees, then gather a handful of leaves, steep them in hot water for 5-10 minutes, and enjoy your tea.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature can be soothing, and the activity allows for flexible pacing.

activity_title: Collect nettle plants for soup
instruction: Wear gloves and carefully find and collect fresh nettle plants. Rinse them, then simmer with water, potatoes, and onions for about 20 minutes to create a nutrient-rich soup.

activity_title: Craft a simple baking soda and vinegar volcano
instruction: In a container, mix 1/4 cup of baking soda with a few drops of food coloring. Pour in 1/2 cup of vinegar and watch your volcano erupt in a fizzy explosion.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and clear steps, visual and auditory feedback, engaging and fun activity

activity_title: Perform a simple chromatography experiment using coffee filters and markers
instruction: Draw a thick line with a marker near the bottom of a coffee filter, then dip the bottom in water without submerging the ink. Watch the colors spread and separate as the water travels up the filter.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and visual activity, low pressure, engaging and colorful process

activity_title: Build a homemade barometer to measure weather changes
instruction: Take a glass jar and stretch a balloon over the top, securing it with a rubber band. Use a straw taped to the balloon to create a pointer on a scale marked on paper to track changes in air pressure.
neurodivergent_notes: Clear, simple steps with visual tracking, hands-on activity, no time constraints

activity_title: Create an egg drop contraption with household materials
instruction: Gather materials like cardboard, tape, and plastic bags. Build a protective structure for an egg and drop it from a safe height to see if it survives.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages creativity and problem-solving with flexible outcomes.

activity_title: Conduct a dissolving experiment with candy
instruction: Gather different types of candy, such as gummy bears, hard candies, and chocolate. Fill three cups with water and three cups with vinegar. Drop a piece of each candy into the cups and observe how they dissolve over time.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and engaging, allows for visual observation and minimal pressure.

activity_title: Design a DIY sundial using sticks and stones
instruction: Gather a straight stick and some stones. Place the stick upright in the ground and arrange the stones in a circle around it to mark the hours. Observe how the shadow moves throughout the day.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and tactile activity, allows for exploration and creativity in a natural setting

activity_title: Construct a simple periscope out of cardboard
instruction: Cut two rectangular pieces of cardboard (about 10 inches by 4 inches) and two small mirrors. Attach the mirrors at a 45-degree angle on opposite ends of the cardboard pieces, then connect them to form a tube. Look through one end to see over obstacles.
neurodivergent_notes: Hands-on activity with clear steps, encourages creativity and problem-solving, no time pressure

activity_title: Explore making invisible ink using lemon juice
instruction: Squeeze the juice of half a lemon into a small bowl. Use a cotton swab or a fine brush to write a message on white paper with the juice. Allow it to dry completely, then gently heat the paper with a hairdryer or by holding it near a light bulb to reveal your secret message.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple, clear steps with visual feedback; engaging and fun to see results; no time pressure.

activity_title: Build a baking soda and vinegar volcano
instruction: On a tray, place a small container and fill it with 1/4 cup of baking soda. Slowly pour in 1/2 cup of vinegar and watch the eruption as it bubbles and fizzes.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and engaging, provides visual stimulation, quick to complete with no pressure.

activity_title: Complete a crossword puzzle using a dictionary for challenging words
instruction: Find a crossword puzzle online or in a book, and keep a dictionary nearby to look up any challenging words as you fill in the grid.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging and structured activity, allows for breaks, and can be done at your own pace.

activity_title: Create a mini treasure hunt in your home
instruction: Write clues that lead to different spots in your home, hiding a small prize at the final location. Start with a simple clue and build up to more challenging ones as you go.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible structure, encourages movement and exploration, can be adapted to individual preferences

activity_title: Design a set of yoga sequences focusing on balance and flexibility
instruction: Create a series of yoga poses that enhance balance and flexibility, such as tree pose, warrior III, and pigeon pose. Practice each pose for 5 breaths, holding them for a total of 15-20 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Structured routine with clear poses, can be adapted for individual comfort levels

activity_title: Start a worm composting bin using kitchen scraps and garden soil
instruction: Gather kitchen scraps like vegetable peels and coffee grounds, mix them with garden soil in a container, and add red wiggler worms. Keep the bin moist and turn it occasionally to aerate.
neurodivergent_notes: Hands-on activity with clear steps, sensory engagement, and no strict time limits.

activity_title: Plant carrot tops in water
instruction: Cut the tops off fresh carrots and place them in a shallow dish filled with water, ensuring the cut ends are submerged. Change the water every few days and watch as new greens sprout.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and predictable process, visual growth provides rewarding feedback, minimal sensory overload

activity_title: Set up a finger painting session with homemade natural dyes from fruits and vegetables
instruction: Create natural dyes by blending fruits and vegetables like beets, spinach, and blueberries with a little water. Set up a space with paper and let your fingers explore the colors as you paint freely.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible and open-ended activity, encourages sensory exploration without strict guidelines.

activity_title: Test the buoyancy of objects in water
instruction: Fill a shallow basin with water and drop in various objects like coins, leaves, and small toys to see which float and which sink. Record your findings.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and engaging task with visual and tactile elements, allows for exploration at your own pace

activity_title: Solve a Sudoku puzzle on paper
instruction: Start with an easy Sudoku puzzle and gradually move to harder ones, using a pencil to fill in numbers while ensuring each row, column, and 3x3 grid contains all digits from 1 to 9 without repetition.
neurodivergent_notes: Structured activity with clear rules, can be done at one's own pace, promotes focus and calmness

activity_title: Host a memory challenge
instruction: Place 5-10 small items on a tray, cover it with a cloth for 1-2 minutes, then uncover and try to recall as many items as you can.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible in pace, encourages memory recall, can be adapted to individual needs.

activity_title: Practice balancing poses like the tree and warrior stance
instruction: Stand tall and shift your weight onto one leg, placing the sole of your other foot on your inner thigh or calf. Hold for 5 breaths, then switch sides. For warrior stance, step back with one foot, bend your front knee, and stretch your arms out wide. Hold for 5 breaths, then switch sides.
neurodivergent_notes: Clear, simple movements that can be done at your own pace, promoting focus and calmness.

activity_title: Make herbal tea using fresh herbs from your garden
instruction: Harvest a handful of fresh herbs from your garden, such as mint or chamomile, and steep them in hot water for 5-10 minutes. Take a moment to enjoy the different aromas as they infuse.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple process with sensory engagement, flexible timing, and calming aromas.

activity_title: Grow an avocado plant by suspending the pit in a glass of water with toothpicks
instruction: Remove the pit from a ripe avocado, rinse it, and insert three toothpicks into the sides. Suspend the pit in a glass of water so the bottom half is submerged, and place it in a sunny spot. Change the water every few days and watch it sprout over the weeks.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and engaging process, visual growth to track, minimal sensory overload

activity_title: Create a sensory garden with diverse herbs and flowers
instruction: Choose a small area in your garden or a few pots. Plant a variety of herbs like lavender, mint, and rosemary, along with flowers like marigolds and lamb's ear for their unique textures. Water them regularly and enjoy the sensory experience as they grow.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with plants can provide calming sensory input and a predictable routine.

activity_title: Mix cornstarch and water to explore the properties of non-Newtonian fluids
instruction: Combine 1 cup of cornstarch with 1/2 cup of water in a bowl, mixing until you achieve a thick, gooey consistency. Use your hands to feel how it behaves like a solid when pressed but flows like a liquid when not under pressure.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and engaging sensory experience, adaptable to different preferences, allows for exploration at one's own pace.

activity_title: Create a logic puzzle involving a sequence of riddles
instruction: Think of a final answer and create 3-5 riddles that lead to it, ensuring each riddle has a clue that connects to the next one. Write them down and challenge a friend or family member to solve them.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages creative thinking and problem-solving at your own pace, with flexible structure.

activity_title: Play a game of chess with a friend or master a difficult chess opening
instruction: Set up a chessboard and challenge a friend to a game, or spend time learning and practicing a specific chess opening like the Sicilian Defense or Ruy Lopez.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging and strategic, allows for flexible pacing and focus on individual moves

activity_title: Try a full yoga routine emphasizing deep breathing and slow, controlled movements
instruction: Begin in a comfortable seated position, take a deep breath in through your nose, and slowly exhale through your mouth. Flow through gentle poses like cat-cow, downward dog, and child's pose, focusing on your breath for 15-20 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movements, focus on breath, adaptable pace, calming environment

activity_title: Design a compost bin using recycled materials
instruction: Gather materials like wooden pallets, plastic bins, or cardboard boxes. Cut and assemble them into a bin, ensuring proper ventilation and drainage. Start composting kitchen scraps and yard waste to create nutrient-rich soil.
neurodivergent_notes: Hands-on activity with clear steps, can be done at own pace, allows for sensory exploration.

activity_title: Sow radish seeds in a pot and track their growth
instruction: Fill a small pot with soil, plant radish seeds about 1 inch apart, cover lightly with soil, and water gently. Place in a sunny spot and check daily to track their growth over several weeks.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging with nature, routine tracking, and gentle sensory experiences can be soothing and grounding.

activity_title: Make a tactile collage using textured materials
instruction: Gather textured materials like fabric, sandpaper, and leaves. Arrange them on a piece of cardboard or paper, gluing them down as you go. Let your creativity flow and enjoy the different textures.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible materials, encourages sensory exploration, no strict rules

activity_title: Create a lava lamp using oil, water, and food coloring
instruction: Fill a clear bottle with water, leaving some space at the top. Add a few drops of food coloring, then slowly pour in vegetable oil until the bottle is nearly full. Watch as the colored water forms bubbles that rise and fall.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and visual, engaging for various sensory preferences, no complex instructions

activity_title: Assemble a jigsaw puzzle
instruction: Select a jigsaw puzzle with numerous pieces and find a comfortable space to spread out the pieces. Start by sorting the edge pieces and then work on connecting them to form the picture, piece by piece.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging and repetitive, allows for focus and breaks, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Create a deck of homemade flashcards for a memory and recall exercise
instruction: Gather index cards or cut cardstock into small rectangles. Write down plant names on one side and their care instructions on the other. Use these cards to quiz yourself and improve your memory.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible pacing, visual and tactile engagement, can be done in short bursts

activity_title: Perform a series of sun salutations outdoors
instruction: Sun salutations are a flowing sequence of yoga poses done in rhythm with your breath. Start standing, raise your arms overhead, fold forward, step back into a plank, flow through to a gentle backbend, and repeat 5 times while enjoying the fresh air.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movement, rhythmic breathing, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Repurpose old pots to build a micro-garden with a variety of herbs
instruction: Gather old pots, fill them with potting soil, and plant a mix of herbs like basil, mint, and parsley. Water them lightly and place them in a sunny spot.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging and repetitive tasks, sensory-rich experience, flexible timing

activity_title: Plant garlic cloves in pots
instruction: Fill a small pot with soil, plant garlic cloves about 2 inches deep, water them lightly, and place the pot in a sunny spot. Watch them sprout over the coming weeks.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle routine, simple steps, engaging with nature, low pressure

activity_title: Craft a sensory path using materials like stones, sand, and fabric for barefoot walking
instruction: Gather materials like smooth stones, soft fabric, and sand. Arrange them in a path on the ground, alternating textures to create a sensory experience for your bare feet.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging multiple senses, customizable path, encourages exploration and movement at one's own pace

activity_title: Make a simple electromagnet
instruction: Wrap insulated copper wire around a large iron nail, leaving some wire free at each end. Connect the ends to a battery and test its strength by picking up small metal objects.

activity_title: Complete a series of logic grid puzzles
instruction: Find a logic grid puzzle online or in a book, read through the clues, and use a pencil to mark your deductions on the grid until you solve it.
neurodivergent_notes: Structured problem-solving, visual organization, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Hold a Scrabble game night using a pre-owned board for vocabulary building
instruction: Gather friends or family and set up a Scrabble board. Each player draws 7 tiles and takes turns forming words on the board, aiming for the highest score. Enjoy the challenge and expand your vocabulary together.
neurodivergent_notes: Encourages social interaction in a structured format, allows for flexible pacing and word choices.

activity_title: Practice yoga poses that open up the chest and enhance circulation
instruction: Start in a comfortable seated position, take a deep breath, and flow through these poses: 1. Cat-Cow (10 rounds), 2. Cobra Pose (hold for 30 seconds), 3. Bridge Pose (hold for 30 seconds), 4. Fish Pose (hold for 1 minute). Focus on your breath and feel your chest expand.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle movements, predictable sequence, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Design a rainwater collection system for your garden using a barrel and gutters
instruction: Gather a rain barrel, gutters, and downspouts. Attach the gutters to your roof's edge, directing water into the barrel. Ensure the barrel has a lid and a spigot for easy access.

activity_title: Create a small windowsill garden by starting seeds in recycled containers
instruction: Gather recycled containers like yogurt cups or egg cartons, fill them with potting soil, and plant seeds according to the packet instructions. Water gently and place them on your windowsill to soak up the sun.
neurodivergent_notes: Hands-on activity with flexible timing, engaging sensory experience, and a calming routine.

activity_title: Sculpt textured shapes with clay or playdough
instruction: Take a small amount of clay or playdough and use your fingers to create various textured shapes, focusing on the feel of the material as you mold it.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging tactile experience, flexible time commitment, promotes relaxation and focus

activity_title: Work through a challenging word search with a focus on unknown words
instruction: Find a word search puzzle online or in a book, and take your time to look for words you don't know. Write down their meanings as you find them to expand your vocabulary.
neurodivergent_notes: Engaging and flexible, allows for breaks and pacing, can be done in a quiet space

activity_title: Develop and solve your own cryptic crossword puzzle
instruction: Create a grid on paper, fill in words based on clues you write for each word, then challenge yourself or a friend to solve it. Aim for 10-15 words to start.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible pacing, can be done in short bursts, encourages creativity and problem-solving

activity_title: Engage in a yoga nidra session for deep relaxation and mental clarity
instruction: Find a quiet, comfortable space to lie down. Close your eyes and take a few deep breaths. Follow a guided yoga nidra recording or simply focus on relaxing each part of your body, starting from your toes to the crown of your head, for 20-40 minutes.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle and predictable practice, focuses on relaxation, can be done in a quiet space without distractions

activity_title: Plan and implement a no-dig raised bed in your garden for easy vegetable growing
instruction: Choose a sunny spot in your garden, outline a rectangular area, layer cardboard or newspaper to suppress weeds, add compost and soil on top, and plant your favorite vegetables directly into the soil.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible timeline, hands-on activity with tangible results, sensory-rich environment, can be done at your own pace

activity_title: Plant a variety of lettuce seeds in a shady spot
instruction: Choose a shady spot in your garden or on your balcony, prepare small pots with potting soil, and plant a few lettuce seeds in each pot, covering them lightly with soil. Water gently and watch them grow.
neurodivergent_notes: Gentle sensory experience, repetitive actions, and a calming connection to nature

activity_title: Create a sensory exploration tray with objects of different temperatures and textures
instruction: Gather items like ice cubes, warm cloths, smooth stones, and rough bark. Place them on a tray and explore the different sensations with your hands and feet.
neurodivergent_notes: Flexible exploration, engaging multiple senses, can be done at one's own pace

activity_title: Construct a simple sundial in your yard
instruction: Find a flat surface in your yard, place a stick or a pencil upright in the center, and mark the shadow's position every hour on a sunny day to track the passage of time.
neurodivergent_notes: Simple and clear steps, engaging with nature, visual tracking of time can be soothing.

activity_title: Craft a cardboard labyrinth and guide a marble through it
instruction: Cut a piece of cardboard into a rectangle, then create walls using strips of cardboard to form a maze. Use a marble to navigate through the labyrinth, testing your dexterity.

activity_title: Participate in a game of charades
